title: An isomorphism of the free group factors
analyst_role: paper (LaTeX) analyst; Lean and reasoning trace not read
base_library_L: Mathlib d13f23b + references.bib of this manuscript (19 entries)

main_statement.paraphrase: The group von Neumann algebras of the free groups on 2 and 3 generators are isomorphic, by a normal *-isomorphism that preserves the canonical traces. This resolves Kadison's free group factor isomorphism problem in the affirmative.

constructive_core.latex:
\begin{theorem}[Isomorphism of consecutive ranks]
\label{thm:rank-step}
For every integer $n\geq3$ there is a unital trace-preserving normal
$*$-isomorphism
\[
 L(\F_n)\cong L(\F_{n+1}).
\]
\end{theorem}
constructive_core.paraphrase: For n >= 3, L(F_{n+1}) contains n unitaries with the free Haar distribution that generate it. Thm main follows by applying this at n=3,4 and amplifying by sqrt(2) with Dykema's formula.

headline_corollaries.paraphrase: All interpolated free group factors L(F_r), 1<r<=infinity, are isomorphic, and each has fundamental group R_{>0}. Uses Radulescu's dichotomy (cited).

None of Voiculescu's free entropy dimensions delta, delta_0, delta^*, delta^star is invariant under change of W*-generators: on L(F_2) each takes every integer value n>=2. This answers Voiculescu's question negatively.

main_statement.note_for_comparator: The headline (Thm main) is NOT proved constructively by itself. It needs the cited Dykema amplification formula. The new mathematics is in Thm rank-step (n>=3). Record both when matching against Lean.

A.label: A2

evidence.quote: There exists a unital normal trace-preserving $*$-isomorphism \Phi:L(\F_2)\longrightarrow L(\F_3).

A.note: This is a pure existence claim for an isomorphism. The rank-step is also of the form for every n>=3 there exists an isomorphism; n only indexes the family. Corollary all-interpolated adds a computation of the fundamental group, which would be A3/A4-like, but it is a corollary.

flags.full_only_with_prior_results_detail: The constructive theorem gives L(F_n)=L(F_{n+1}) only for n>=3. Reaching rank 2 needs Dykema's amplification formula [dykema1994, Thm 2.4]. The corollaries for every interpolated factor, L(F_infinity) and the fundamental group need Radulescu's dichotomy [radulescu1994, Cor 4.7].
flags.adds_corollaries_detail: It answers negatively Voiculescu's question on whether free entropy dimension is a W*-invariant [voiculescu2002entropy, Sec 2.6], in all four variants. The fundamental group R_{>0} is new for finite r. For L(F_infinity) it was already known [radulescu1992].

items.name: bounded Borel logarithm S=arg(C) and its conjugates S_g=A_g S A_g^*
items.statement: Take the Borel logarithm of the free Haar generator C, with values in (-pi,pi], so that S is self-adjoint, centered, ||S||<=pi and e^{iS}=C. Then conjugate S by the group words in A.

cited_or_new.status: functional calculus cited; use is new to this argument

load_bearing_guess.reason: S drives the flow. A Borel (non-continuous) log is essential: C is exponentially connected to 1 in B=C*(A,S) but not in C*_r(F_{n+1}) (K_1). That is how the argument avoids the C*-level obstruction.

provisional_N.justification: The bounded log of a free Haar unitary, giving C^t=exp(itS), is exactly the ingredient of Popa's free malleable deformation (Ioana-Peterson-Popa 2008). The conjugate family is the free Bernoulli field of F_n.

items.name: Polynomial flow and displacement bounds (prop:flow)
items.statement: There is a one-parameter group beta_t of trace-preserving normal automorphisms of M fixing S, with ||beta_t(A_j)-A_j|| <= |t| K ||h_j||_2 and ||beta_t(A_w) - e^{itS} A_w|| <= |t| K ||D_w - delta_e||_2.

cited_or_new.cue: We prove the version needed here directly for Haar unitaries and a fixed bounded logarithm.

load_bearing_guess.reason: It reduces the operator-algebra problem to a linear coefficient problem in ell^2(F_n). The bound is exact, not first-order: s_t(k)=beta_t(s(k)), so a naive product-of-exponentials (BCH) error of order m*eta^2=O(1) never arises.

provisional_N.justification: The leaning is N3. Its parts have close precedents: cyclomorphy (named), Popa's free malleable deformation and Sinclair / Peterson-Sinclair Gaussian cocycle deformations (not named). What appears new is the word-displacement bound in operator norm, inside M itself, with no ambient dilation.

cited_or_new.cue: The coefficient problem is solved in Lemma~\ref{lem:small-cocycle} (main.tex:99)

load_bearing_guess.reason: Without it the flow cannot absorb C. It is exactly where non-amenability enters: it fails for F_1=Z, where Dirichlet kernels make it impossible, and for property (T) groups, where small cocycles are small coboundaries.

provisional_N.justification: Weak N3. Posing the problem (generator values small in ell^2 while one word value approximates delta_e) is non-analytic and seems new. Once posed, the solution is textbook free probability: circular law and spectral cutoff. So the pivot is one step from L, and a judge may grade it N2.

proof_architecture.claim: Setup: M=L(F_{n+1}) with canonical free Haar tuple (A,C). Take S=arg C and the conjugates S_g, which form a free family. The free sum s(k) has norm <= 3 pi ||k||_2.

Cocycle flow: for real finitely supported h_j, the ODE A_j' = i s_t(h_j) A_j has global unitary solutions. tau composed with ev_0 and delta vanishes on the formal algebra, by first variation and freeness. Analyticity then gives moment invariance, hence trace-preserving automorphisms beta_t fixing S. Exact bounds: ||beta_1(A_j)-A_j|| <= K||h_j|| and ||beta_1(A_w) - C A_w|| <= K||D_w - delta_e||.

Coefficient problem: with w_m = p_m x_1 built from free prefixes, D_{w_m} = T_m h. T_m T_m^*/m tends to free Poisson, which has no atom at 0. A cutoff inverse plus truncation gives ||h|| < eta and ||D_w - delta_e|| < eta.
One-step absorption: alpha = gamma^{-1} beta_1, with gamma the Nielsen move C -> C A_w. Then alpha(A) is eps-close to A and alpha(A)_w is eps-close to C. The new completion is C A_w^*.

Iterate with adaptive budgets: approximate a dense sequence y_j in the current tuple, perturb, substitute the witness word, then fix the future budget. A^(k) converges in norm to a free Haar n-tuple whose word algebra is L^2-dense. The conditional expectation then gives W*(A^(inf)) = M, which proves Thm rank-step for n>=3.
Headline: N_3=N_4=N_5. Amplify by sqrt 2 with Dykema's formula (cited) to get L(F_2)=L(F_3).
Corollaries: Radulescu's dichotomy (cited) makes all L(F_r), 1<r<=inf, isomorphic, with fundamental group R_{>0}. Transporting tuples refutes W*-invariance of the four free entropy dimensions.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found on a line-by-line reading of all six sections. This is an extraordinary claim and remains unreviewed, so it needs expert and Lean confirmation.
checked: Lemma conjugates: the cyclic rewrite is valid, including the case g_r=g_1. Dropping the identity factor still leaves a valid alternating centered product.
Free-sum bound: L_z = B + B^* + diagonal, with (1-P_j)L(1-P_j)=0. The constant 2*pi + pi = 3*pi is correct, since ||S||_2 = pi/sqrt3 <= pi.

Trace identity: delta preserves labels. Identity-label monomials rewrite as polynomials in z_g inside P, which is valid because F_n has no relators. The conjugation by exp(iuY_g), Y_g in W*(S_b : b != g), preserves the joint law. The sum of first variations equals tau(ev_0(delta p)). Since this holds on all of P, iterating gives all orders.
Moment invariance: the factorial bound is uniform in t, so f_p is real-analytic on R with vanishing derivatives at 0.
Word-displacement bound is exact: d/dt(e^{-itS}A_w(t)) = i e^{-itS}(s_t(D_w)-S)A_w(t), and ||s_t(k)|| = ||beta_t(s(k))||. There is no BCH/first-order error.
Coefficient lemma: D_{w_m} = sum_{j=0}^m lambda(p_j) h. The limit law is free Poisson. ||h^(0)||^2 = tau(R_m) <= 1/(dm).
Prop. perturbation: alpha(A_w) - C = gamma^{-1}(beta(A_w) - C A_w). Correct.
Generation: the order of choices makes L_k r_k <= 2^{-k}. The conditional-expectation argument is standard.
Amplification arithmetic is correct for t = sqrt 2.
consistency_checks_passed: K-theory: K_1(C*_r F_n) = Z^n distinguishes the reduced C*-algebras. The flow lives on B = C*(A, arg C), where C = e^{iS} is null-homotopic, and the limit only generates at the W* level. So there is no conflict, and the Borel (non-continuous) logarithm is necessary.
No over-reach to amenable groups: for F_1 = Z the coefficient problem is impossible (Dirichlet-kernel obstruction), so the argument cannot give L(Z) = L(F_2).

No over-reach to property (T): for (T) groups every ell^2 cocycle is a coboundary with ||xi|| <= kappa^{-1} max_j ||b(x_j)||, so small generator values force small word values. The analog of L(G)*L(Z) = L(G) is blocked. Groups with relators also break the trace identity, because P has no relators.

No over-reach to commutative Gaussian analogs: without freeness of C the Nielsen automorphism gamma does not exist. Otherwise one would contradict Voiculescu's theorem that L(F_n) has no Cartan subalgebra.
residual_concerns: The result conflicts with the prevailing expectation, and it disproves W*-invariance of delta_0, which many believed. These are not contradictions with any theorem I know, but they raise the bar for verification.

The closest precedent, shlyakhtenko2026fuchsian (arXiv 2609.11074, 10 Sep 2026), postdates our knowledge cutoff and cannot be checked here. Neither its content nor its human or model provenance is known.
Popa / Ioana-Peterson-Popa free malleable deformations and Sinclair / Peterson-Sinclair Gaussian cocycle deformations are not cited, although they are the closest conceptual neighbours of the flow.

Corollary on free entropy: delta_0 of semicirculars is cited to Brannan-Elzinga-Harris-Yamashita 2023 rather than Voiculescu's original. The claim delta^* = delta^star for group generators should be checked against the exact statement of Mineyev-Shlyakhtenko Thm 4.1.
The constructive step needs n>=3 (it uses x_2, x_3 in addition to a = x_1). Rank 2 rests entirely on Dykema's amplification formula, which is a standard and reliable theorem.

extraction_friction: Several load-bearing objects are introduced in display math or prose with no \emph and no environment: s(k), the cocycle D, the formal algebra P and derivation delta, the vector field V_j, the prefix words w_m and T_m, the cutoff inverse R_m, the Nielsen automorphism gamma, and the budget scheme. A naive extractor misses the core machinery. The only inline \emph definitions are normal, free, label and completion.

Key sub-claims sit inside proofs as unnumbered paragraphs: unitary conjugation preserves freeness (flow.tex:155-167), norm from moments (flow.tex:344-353), and the Nielsen automorphism (generation.tex:56-65).
The headline theorem (thm:main) is a corollary of the constructive theorem (thm:rank-step, n>=3) plus a cited formula. The Lean comparator could target either.
Section order in main.tex (flow, then cocycle) differs from the order in the introduction narrative (cocycle described first). Theorem counters are shared per section.
